news.headline: “If you want to turn ideas into reality, this is the place to do it”
Sustainability is no longer a promise, it is an operational question
The growing mobility challenge nobody can staff their way out of
Autonomous transport is an integrated system, not a standalone vehicle

paragraphs: 2getthere builds automated transit vehicles that carry passengers with no driver on board. The systems are sold for smart cities, airports, campuses and industrial zones, and for urban and rural transit applications.

Because the vehicles run in a lane of their own, the company presents them as a way to move more people without adding to road congestion. In cities the service is aimed at the first and last mile, feeding passengers to metro, rail and bus. Other settings named on the site include business parks, universities, theme parks and ports.

The company describes its staff as Utrecht-based engineers, operators and systems-thinkers working on autonomous transit. It traces its work on new transit systems back to 1999. A route at Rivium outside Rotterdam has run driverless vehicles in daily service for more than a quarter-century. One entry in the company timeline reports transporting over 2.7 million passengers to date.
